fixes.explanation: Jesus says, “Let us cross to the other side of the lake.” Clear plan, clear destination, no confusion. I've gotten turned around between my own counter and my own oven, so a plan that clean impresses me.
Yes, Jesus “…rebuked the wind and the raging waters…” Then they subsided, and all was calm. He doesn't sit and watch the storm. He gets up and speaks to it, and it settles.

Watching isn't what the text says. It says Jesus got up and “…rebuked the wind and the raging waters…” Then they subsided, and all was calm. He doesn't just sit through the storm. He gets up and speaks to it.

Yes, the text says, “Frightened and amazed, they asked one another…” The storm is gone, but the fear isn't. Calm water, shaken disciples. I think they'd just seen something they couldn't file away anywhere.

That one's not in the text. It says, “Frightened and amazed, they asked one another…” Anger isn't the word the text gives. It gives fear and amazement, and I think they were wondering about what they'd just watched.
The text has them asking something else. It says, “Who is this? He commands even the winds and the water, and they obey Him!” That question is about Jesus. It isn't about the route.

“Son of David” is a title people call Jesus in Matthew 9:27, but it's not what this man shouts. He says, “What do You want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God?” That's the name that comes out of him, loud and clear.

Yes, “…he had broken the chains…” They were chains and shackles, and still they didn't hold him. The text says he was driven by the demon into solitary places. I think this part of the story is heavy.

They didn't hold. The text says that though he was bound with chains and shackles, “…he had broken the chains…” The demon drove him into solitary places. I think this one is heavy, so I'll say it plainly.
Nobody unlocked them. The text says, “…he had broken the chains…” They didn't hold him, and he was driven by the demon into solitary places. I think this is a heavy part of the story.

Yes, “…the demons begged Jesus to let them enter the pigs…” Right before that, the demons kept begging Jesus not to order them to go into the Abyss (Luke 8:31). A large herd of pigs was feeding on the hillside. That's what they asked about.
Yes, “…He gave them permission.” The demons begged to enter the pigs, and Jesus gave His permission. The text says it plainly, and so will I. True.
The text says the opposite. The demons begged to enter the pigs, “…and He gave them permission.” So Jesus did give permission. That makes this one True.

Yes, “…the herd rushed down the steep bank into the lake and was drowned.” This happens after the demons came out of the man and went into the pigs. It's a hard scene, and the text tells it plainly. Then those tending the pigs ran off and reported it in the town and countryside.
Yes, “…they were afraid.” The people find the man sitting at Jesus' feet, clothed and in his right mind. I'd have expected cheering, but the text says fear. That's what they felt.

Yes, “…all the people of the region of the Gerasenes asked Jesus to depart from them, because great fear had taken hold of them.” The text gives their fear as the reason. So Jesus got into the boat and started back. That's how this stop ends.

Yes! Jesus says, “Return home and describe how much God has done for you.” The man had just begged to go with Jesus, and Jesus sends him home instead. Home, where he lived among the tombs before, is where he gets to tell it. And he does, proclaiming all over the town how much Jesus had done for him.
